chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was brought a thief who had stolen dirhams from the sleeve of a man's garment. He said: 'If it was from his outer shirt, I would not cut his hand, but if it was from his inner shirt, I would cut his hand.'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for cutting the thief's hand according to Imam Ali regarding stolen goods from clothing?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's chain highlights the jurisprudential nuance in calculating the minimum value (nisab) for hand amputation, where the Imam distinguishes between the outer and inner garments to determine if the threshold is met. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise material valuation in hudud punishments, ensuring the penalty is applied only when the stolen item's worth exceeds the specific standard derived from the victim's attire.
